ledger.note: 1740: Pegu rises against Ava and the Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom begins. 'The Ava-appointed governor at Pegu was assassinated on 29 November' and on 8 December the court elected Smim Htaw Buddhaketi king. The page names Pegu; the extent over Lower Burma is the first-toungoo-empire dossier's reading (Cliopatria's Konbaung 1741 shape). Repair: the region no longer includes Mon, Kayin and Tanintharyi, which the page says did not belong to the kingdom ('sought and received Siamese protection'; 'did not control the northern Tenasserim coast').

region.text: Prome and Toungoo, the Bago region without Pegu

ledger.note: 1742: Mon raids up the Irrawaddy begin. 'Hanthawaddy forces began annual raids up the Irrawaddy as far as Ava' from 1742, which contests Prome and Toungoo until 1745.

region.text: Prome and Toungoo, the Bago region without Pegu

ledger.note: 1745: the raids end in conquest of Prome and Toungoo. 'By 1745, Hanthawaddy controlled much of Lower Burma, and parts of Upper Burma up to Prome and Toungoo.'

region.text: Prome and Toungoo, the Bago region without Pegu

ledger.note: 1745: Prome and Toungoo pass to the Mon kingdom. 'By 1745, Hanthawaddy controlled much of Lower Burma, and parts of Upper Burma up to Prome and Toungoo.' The page gives the year of the result, not of each town.

region.text: Upper Burma around Sagaing and Ava

ledger.note: 1751: Binnya Dala invades Upper Burma. In November 1751 he 'launched a full-scale invasion of Upper Burma'.

region.text: Upper Burma north of Ava, where Alaungpaya rose

ledger.note: 1752: Alaungpaya's rising begins the Konbaung-Hanthawaddy War. The Konbaung dossier opens the contest in April 1752; the Hanthawaddy page dates the founding of the Konbaung Dynasty to March 1752.

minus.text: Ava (Inwa) and Sagaing across the river

region.text: Upper Burma north of Ava

ledger.note: 1752: Alaungpaya clears Upper Burma north of Ava. He 'drove out Hanthawaddy outposts north of Ava' by October 1752 (war page); the Hanthawaddy page puts the reconquest of 'Upper Burma north of Ava' in December 1752; 'by late 1753, Konbaung controlled all of Upper Burma except Ava'. The Konbaung dossier dates its gain to 1753.

region.text: Ava and the Toungoo realm of 1751

ledger.note: March 1752: Ava falls to the Mons. 'In March 1752, Hanthawaddy forces sacked Ava, ending the Toungoo dynasty'; the royal family was taken to Pegu. The Mons never held the whole 1751 outline: see the 1752 loss north of Ava.

region.text: Upper Burma around Sagaing and Ava

ledger.note: March 1752: the Toungoo dynasty ends with the sack of Ava; the fight over Upper Burma is now with Alaungpaya.

region.text: Upper Burma north of Ava, where Alaungpaya rose

ledger.note: 1754: Upper Burma is secure. Ava retaken in January 1754 and the Mon army driven back to Sagaing by May 1754.

region.text: Prome (Pyay)

ledger.note: 1754: Prome turns against the Mons. 'Burman refugees who had escaped general slaughter by the delta Mons seized Prome (Pyay) ... and shut the gates to the retreating Hanthawaddy armies' (war page, no year in the sentence; it follows the 1754 retreat from Upper Burma, so the year is a reading); a Hanthawaddy army under Talaban besieged it.

region.text: Prome (Pyay)

ledger.note: 1754: Prome lost to Burman refugees who sided with Alaungpaya. The war page names the town but gives no year in the sentence (it follows the 1754 retreat); the counterpart is Konbaung, which relieved the siege. Confidence lowered from 3 to 2 by the se-01-x reviewer.

region.text: Ava (Inwa), left 'ruined and burned'

ledger.note: 3 January 1754: Ava retaken. Hsinbyushin 'successfully retook Ava, which was left ruined and burned' (war page). The Hanthawaddy page says 1753, a year earlier: the war page's date is used.

region.text: the invasion of Lower Burma

ledger.note: April 1755: Alaungpaya invades the delta. 'Alaungpaya launched the delta invasion in early April.'

region.text: Taungoo (Toungoo)

ledger.note: 1755: Toungoo submits to Alaungpaya. Binnya Dala page: 'Alaugpaya then swept southward with his grand army receiving submission from Taungoo...', placed after the relief of Pyay (February 1755) and before the capture of the delta (May 1755); the sentence has no year, so the year is a reading from the order. The Alaungpaya page says only that he later 'appointed ... another at Taungoo' as viceroy. The Konbaung–Hanthawaddy War page has a Konbaung army marching 'from Toungoo' in September 1756.

region.text: Prome (Pyay)

ledger.note: February 1755: the siege of Prome is lifted. Alaungpaya 'captured the Mayanbin fort, relieving the siege' in mid-February 1755.

region.text: the Irrawaddy Delta and Dagon (Yangon)

ledger.note: 1755: the delta and Dagon fall. 'By late April, his forces had overrun the entire delta'; 'On 5 May 1755, Konbaung troops defeated a Hanthawaddy division at Dagon.' Syriam, across the river, stayed Mon until July 1756.

region.text: Syriam (Thanlyin), the French-garrisoned port across the river from Dagon

ledger.note: 26 July 1756: Syriam falls. The French-defended port fell 'at dawn on 26 July 1756, after bloody hand-to-hand fighting'; two French relief ships arrived on 29 July, 'a few days too late'.

region.text: Pegu and its country: the Bago region without Prome and Toungoo, the last land the kingdom held

ledger.note: 6 May 1757: Pegu falls. 'Konbaung armies broke through at moonrise, and massacred men, women, and children without distinction.' Infobox: 'Konbaung annexes Lower Burma down to upper Tenasserim peninsula'; The Konbaung annexation of 'Lower Burma down to upper Tenasserim peninsula' is wider than the Mon kingdom's last land: Martaban and Tavoy, which had sought Siamese protection, were not Pegu's to lose (Alaungpaya page: 'In the south too, the governors of Mottama and Dawei also sent tribute').

region.text: Pegu falls

ledger.note: 6 May 1757: the Konbaung-Hanthawaddy War ends in a 'Decisive Konbaung victory'.

belligerents: Kingdom of Ayutthaya (backing Martaban and Tavoy)

wars.outcome: Decisive Konbaung victory: Ava retaken in January 1754, the delta overrun in April-May 1755, Syriam taken in July 1756, Pegu in May 1757; Konbaung annexes Lower Burma.
wars.note: Hanthawaddy's March 1754 invasion of Upper Burma failed. Martaban and Tavoy 'had sought Siamese protection' and backed off only after Pegu fell.

certainty.note: The Mon frontier with Ava shifts with each campaign and no page gives a boundary; the southern and eastern edge (the Mon coast at Martaban, and Tenasserim) is the least certain: the page says only that the kingdom 'did not control the northern Tenasserim coast'.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks: the Mon kingdom of 1740-1757 appears only as the stray Konbaung Dynasty row 1741-1751 (116,345 km2), which konbaung-dynasty has marked wrong. Two pages opened in the first run (budget), two more in the repair pass. Settled in the repair pass (2026-10-19): the shape no longer includes Mon, Kayin and Tanintharyi (the Martaban and Tavoy country). Restored_Hanthawaddy_Kingdom: 'The new kingdom did not control the northern Tenasserim coast. The rulers of Martaban (Mottama) and Tavoy (Dawei) sought and received Siamese protection.' The Alaungpaya page puts Mon resistance on 'the upper Tenasserim coast (present-day Mon State)' and has 'the governors of Mottama and Dawei' sending tribute only after Bago fell in 1757, so neither was Pegu's own land. The Kayin hills are named by no page; they were removed with the Martaban country because the 1738 outline cut them on that side, so this is conservative. The KF0 shape falls from about 73,100 to 36,700 km2. first-toungoo-empire's 1740-11 loss region (Bago, Yangon, Ayeyarwady, Mon, Kayin, Tanintharyi) should be trimmed to match, or it gives up land that no one then holds. Toungoo: the Binnya Dala page has Alaungpaya 'receiving submission from Taungoo' after the relief of Pyay (February 1755) and before the delta; no year in the sentence, so a 1755 loss at confidence 2 and KF5-KF6 drop it. konbaung-dynasty has no matching gain for Toungoo in 1755 (a 60 km circle) nor for Prome in 1754-55 (Burman refugees seized it; relieved February 1755). Still open: (1) the Hanthawaddy page dates the retaking of Ava to 1753 and the reconquest north of Ava to December 1752, the war page to 3 January 1754 and October 1752: the war page is followed and the konbaung-dynasty dossier's 1753 gain north of Ava is a year later than the 1752 loss here; (2) a page that gives the 1740s Mon-Siamese border at Martaban and Tavoy; the Binnya Dala page is silent on Siamese protection and says Talaban was caught at Mottama in 1757; (3) the Prome counterpart is konbaung-dynasty although Burman refugees took the city; they have no dossier. Reviewer's finding on ledger 10-11 (Prome confidence 3 to 2, quote as written) was applied by the reviewer and kept. Disagreement: none with the fixes; the reviewer's 'thin' hint to open Alaungpaya for Toungoo returned nothing on the town (only the viceroy), the Binnya Dala page gave the sentence.
